samples.question: The picture is a pale instrument sheet carrying exactly six pure-black horizontal bars, arranged as two bars on each of three well-separated levels. No two black bars touch, and the two bars of one level are always separated by blank paper. Every coloured mark - blue, green, orange, purple or grey, whether a bar or a speck - is decoration and carries no information. Only the horizontal extent of each black bar matters: a vertical line crosses a black bar when it passes through the columns that bar covers, and the level a bar sits on is irrelevant. Imagine sliding a single vertical line all the way across the sheet and, at every position, counting how many of the six black bars it crosses. What is the largest count reached at any position? Answer with a single whole number: 1, 2, or 3.
